title: Genetics and the structure of DNA
summary: In 1865 Gregor Mendel presented his pea experiments in Brno; ignored at the time, they were rediscovered in 1900. Thomas Hunt Morgan's fruit fly studies confirmed that genes lie in chromosomes. Oswald Avery's laboratory showed DNA to be the stuff of genes by 1944. In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix, drawing on X-ray images by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin. The Human Genome Project (1990–2003) then produced the first sequence of the human genome.
